rv.q: The gloriously gory, sleek, over-the-top musical that opened Thursday at the Gerald Schoenfeld Theatre is a darkly wonderful adaptation of the once-controversial novel by Bret Easton Ellis.
The show is a very sharp, distinctly theatrical treatment of its source material, in many ways improving on Mary Harron's movie version from 2000.

The sum of these effects is to create a celebration of vapidity and inhumanity that is itself vapid and inhuman.

Of course, it could be argued that the “American Psycho” team has done its job too well, since you’re also likely to identify with Patrick when, shortly before he crucifies a young woman with a nail gun, he concludes solemnly that there’s “not one clear, identifiable emotion within me.”
Still, the result is oddly evanescent, so sleek and gym-toned that any real stab at meaning or consequence slides off and away.
“American Psycho” is slick, sleek and empty, a one-joke show that drowns its message, such as it is, in red sauce and fake emotion.

The triumph of this American Psycho, directed with gale force and fabulous style by Rupert Goold, is that it doesn't get lost in the details informing its brilliant, brutal satire.

Or to put it another way: What might have sounded on paper like an ill-advised stunt — "Let's make a show about a man losing his bearings and slaughtering dozens of people!" — ends up being the timeliest, most trenchant show of the season.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this stylish but shallow adaptation, praising Benjamin Walker's star turn and the sleek '80s aesthetic while faulting Duncan Sheik's forgettable score and questioning whether the material works as a musical at all.

vs.sum: The Gerald Schoenfeld Theatre offers good sightlines with minimal obstructions, although some side seats may have partial views. The sound quality is generally strong, enhancing the theatrical experience. However, the seating is tight, which can affect comfort, particularly for taller patrons. The theater's ambiance is charming with its historic character, and while facilities are adequate, expect some lines at the bar and restrooms.

acc.note: 7 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. Infrared devices available.
